title: Does vibecoding isometric 3d game is really easier than 2d?
author: Disastrous-Ad-6431
selftext: So we got meshy/tripo etc. Is it really that much easier with claude? Im struggling with 2d 32x32px sprites and start to think switching to 3d.

comments.author: CodeWizardCS
comments.body: I feel like it is because you can just tell an agent to use blender. Maybe you can do the same thing with a sprite program. But, messing with imagegen is where 2d gets annoying. There has to be a way but I never figured it out. But, I really like the 3d/2.5d workflow, it's chill. Maybe to get professional level stuff it is difficult.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
I only have experience with trying to gen 2d pixel art but lord it doesn’t seem as straightforward as you would expect. It’s either not pixel perfect or generic as hell.

I kind of like process of editing and make some of my own though because it feels like I’m getting past the “ai slop” look just from having to do so much manually.

Just recently I have seen impressive results that other people have generated though.

comments.author: Economy_Bedroom3902
comments.body: I would think 2D would still be "easier".  AI modeling tools are relatively primitive still compared to image gen...  Although image gen also has a lot of limitations for game dev because it's good at snapshots moreso than animations.

replies.author: CodeWizardCS
replies.body: My agent's seem to excel at 3d modeling and animating. Maybe I don't know how to evaluate quality though.

replies.author: Economy_Bedroom3902
replies.body:
1. My experience is that agents modeling/animating is impressive for how fast and functional it is... but it still makes many mistakes which would not be acceptable for a professional human modeler.  
2. I wasn't trying to shit on modeling agents, there has just been quite a lot longer for agents working in 2D space to improve.  I don't actually know what are the best services/systems/pipelines to use for AI to generate 2D game content though.  Traditional diffus models are bad at coherent animation, but the video models certainly would be a game changer in that space...  You'd want a pipeline to automatically break a video output into keyframes etc however, otherwise it's still a relatively large amount of manual work.  Someone out there must have put together something like this, and probably is offering it as a service/system others can use or download.  I can't believe I'm the first to imagine such a workflow.

replies.author: Anuiran
replies.body: 2D has always been harder. Even before AI

comments.author: josh_the_dev
comments.body: You can always use a 3D block out as basis for your 2D sprite. A lot of games actually have 3D models and just render them into sprites for more consistent 8 direction views for example. I'd say it depends on the game but generally speaking 2D is easier. It's always faster to make and you can get away with much more "cheating". Totally depends on the art style and game though

replies.author: Stxxicorno
replies.body: this is what i am doing. i feel it makes it so much easier as you just need the mesh and textures you like throw them into blender and animate then take images in 8 directions. it so much easier than something like minimax or other image to video then extracting and allows much greater consistency

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
If you use pre-made models, go for it.

I’ve had not so good experiences using Meshy and trying to get good animations (like, go from Meshy to Mixamo, or workflows like that).

Be aware that 3D is harder. That is just life.

comments.author: Disastrous-Ad-6431
comments.body: My main problem is creating good maps with objects, each tile is 32x32 px and creating obejct with pixellab is really hard, they look like flying objects instead of staying on the ground

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Might be an issue with how you make games, not with the LLM.

comments.author: Haster
comments.body: I've had very different difficulties trying both approaches. You'd think 2d would be easier but whole new crop of problems show up. Bit annoying since I don't really care if I go 3d or 2d

comments.author: Varrianda
comments.body:
IMO yes. My serious project is a 2d pixelart MMO which I use actual artists for. I probably could start using their art as a reference but that feels dirty.

You can get surprisingly good 3d art that stays stylistically consistent using Claude/codex and meshy/tripo

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey, Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. I wouldn’t say 3D is automatically easier, just that the bottlenecks move.

With 2D you’re fighting consistency across sprites, poses, and animation frames. With 3D, tools like Tripo can get you to a base asset quickly, but then you still have rigging, animation, scale, camera, materials, and optimization.

For an isometric game though, 3D can be attractive because once the model/rig is working you can reuse it from any angle instead of generating every sprite direction separately.

What part of the 32x32 workflow is giving you the most trouble right now: consistency, animation, or getting the style right?

comments.author: Total-Box-5169
comments.body:
Yes. Nowadays, thanks to game engines, is easier to go 3D. Historically 2D isometric was necessary for performance reasons and each game solved those problems in different ways fit for different games.  
LLMs will have a much easier time generating code that relies on a game engine that already solves most of the hard problems. Otherwise it will have to generate code for the game, and for a 2d isometric game engine.  
Note that isometric art assets usually were rendered from 3D models, while pixel art was preferred for top-down and oblique projection.

comments.author: FailedGradAdmissions
comments.body:
Technically and skills wise 3D is more difficult than 2D. But we are using AI, and as of this exact moment people hate any sort of 2D AI generated art, while they can’t honestly tell apart AI generated low poly from actual low poly. And on top of that there’s thousands of low poly asset packs that you could purchase and have your LLM utilize.

It’ll be incredibly difficult to have AI generate all of your 2D sprites while being cohesive, aesthetically pleasing and also not looking AI generated which people hate. So yeah go 3D.

And sure it’s still doable, but I haven’t really seen one good game with all AI generated 2D sprites. So you’ll get people here that’ll say to you “skill issue” while having nothing to prove it.

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: Go 100% procedural, stop wasting time on game assets! 🔥
